You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From c530189905efe91b6a464db4ec1b56b4c069609f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Xin Long <lucien.xin@gmail.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2020 17:32:03 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] tipc: not enable tipc when ipv6 works as a module

When using ipv6_dev_find() in one module, it requires ipv6 not to
work as a module. Otherwise, this error occurs in build:

  undefined reference to `ipv6_dev_find'.

So fix it by adding "depends on IPV6 || IPV6=n" to tipc/Kconfig,
as it does in sctp/Kconfig.

Fixes: 5a6f6f579178 ("tipc: set ub->ifindex for local ipv6 address")
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Acked-by: Randy Dunlap <rdunlap@infradead.org>
Signed-off-by: Xin Long <lucien.xin@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/tipc/Kconfig b/net/tipc/Kconfig
index 9dd780215eef..be1c4003d67d 100644
--- a/net/tipc/Kconfig
+++ b/net/tipc/Kconfig
@@ -6,6 +6,7 @@
 menuconfig TIPC
 	tristate "The TIPC Protocol"
 	depends on INET
+	depends on IPV6 || IPV6=n
 	help
 	  The Transparent Inter Process Communication (TIPC) protocol is
 	  specially designed for intra cluster communication. This protocol
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/tipc/Kconfig`**
   - Added a new dependency line: `depends on IPV6 || IPV6=n` to the TIPC configuration. This change ensures that the TIPC module can only be enabled if IPv6 is either built into the kernel or not configured as a module.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in the `net/tipc/Kconfig` file addresses a build issue related to the use of the `ipv6_dev_find()` function. By enforcing the dependency on IPv6, the patch prevents the situation where TIPC could be enabled while IPv6 is compiled as a module, which would lead to an undefined reference error during the build process. This change aligns TIPC's configuration with that of the SCTP protocol, which has a similar dependency requirement.

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `ipv6_dev_find()` function is used in the TIPC module, which requires IPv6 to be available in the kernel. If IPv6 is compiled as a module, it leads to an undefined reference error during the build process, as the function cannot be resolved. This situation arises when TIPC is enabled without ensuring that IPv6 is either built into the kernel or not configured as a module.

The `ipv6_dev_find()` function is called in the TIPC module, which requires IPv6 to be available in the kernel. The dependency on `IPV6` without ensuring it is not a module causes this issue.

The code statements that fix the bug are:

This prevents the situation where `ipv6_dev_find()` is called when IPv6 is not available, thus resolving the undefined reference error during the build process.
